subject: Report: Islamic Groups Urged Violence, Called America ‘Satan’ — And Got $47 Million From Taxpayers
posts:
A new report targets Michigan mosques for extremist sermons, but weaponizes school lunch grants to spark political outrage.
Evidence: MEF report, USDA funding, political smears.
#Aletheia #MediaWatch

The Federalist report claims millions in taxpayer funds are subsidizing radical Islamist institutions that preach anti-American violence.
Stated Judgement: (+0.50, +0.00) — Lesser Good

In reality, partisan watchdogs weaponize fringe sermon quotes to defund vital school meal programs and smear Muslim candidates and groups.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.75, -0.65) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Awakening into Destruction.
A watchdog report selectively compiles rhetoric to attack broad community welfare and political rivals.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 13.8, z: 4)

- The Federalist: FAIL (-0.9, -0.8) — Amplifies selective outrage for partisan impact.
- MEF Report: COND (-0.6, -0.5) — Documents real rhetoric but weaponizes it against welfare.
Middle East Forum released a database highlighting controversial statements at Michigan mosques, calling for federal funding freezes.

The Poison:
Valid concerns over extremist rhetoric are co-opted to slash universal nutrition programs and smear political candidates via association.

Plane Error:
Confusing a theological audit (WHAT) with broad administrative welfare distribution (WHO). A few fringe sermon clips do not invalidate essential school lunch programs.

Social Physics Analysis:
Actors execute a Smart Selfish Maneuver by linking fringe statements to mainstream school meal funds, manufacturing a crisis to defund community programs and damage political opponents.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening into Destruction.
Modal Dynamics: will be -> is not via Red Top (The Imperial Trap).
Promising accountability, the report systematically erases nuance to justify cutting welfare.

The Unavoidable Truth: Extremist rhetoric exists in some religious pulpits.

The Unavoidable Lie: Routine school lunch funding constitutes state sponsorship of terrorism.

Alethekanon:
Weaponizing isolated fringe sermon clips to defund universal child nutrition programs is a classic maneuver of partisan extraction.

Awwthekanon:
It breaks my heart when children's school meals and communities are targeted by political crossfire and generalized suspicion.

Brothekanon:
Wild how they take a few sketchy quotes and try to cancel school lunch money for whole communities. Classic hit piece.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment." John 7:24 PASS
Surface outrage must not blind us to the cruelty of cutting bread from the mouths of the innocent.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Report: Islamic Groups Urged Violence, Called America ‘Satan’ — And Got $47 Million From Taxpayers

Abdul El-Sayed has appeared at a number of the mosques and institutions listed.

Actual Article Body:
Abdul El-Sayed has appeared at a number of the mosques and institutions listed.

At more than 30 Islamist institutions in Michigan, speakers demonized America, prayed for jihad, called for the death of Jews, or made other extremist and controversial statements, a new report has found. But a number of these institutions received the approbation of public officials, and a third of these groups raked in nearly $50 million in public funds.

The Middle East Forum, a group focused on “protect[ing] Western values from Islamist threats,” compiled the statements and financial data and published a database of videos of more than 900 statements made at the Islamic institutions, along with an interactive map, lists of funding sources and amounts, and individual pages detailing the institutions. The site is titled “Michigan’s Islamist Pulpits.”

According to an MEF press release, “The site sets out 928 statements from 36 Michigan Islamist institutions, each linked to the institution’s own video at the moment the words were spoken. Twelve of the 36 received $47,357,045 in federal, state, and city money. Forty-one public officials and public bodies attended, spoke at, honored, or funded them in 63 acts.”

MEF captured various kinds of public extremist and anti-American statments. Multiple speakers at certain Islamic institutions have demonized the United States as “the house of shaitan” (Satan), the “great Satan,” or “the belly of the beast,” according to the report. At the Islamic Center of East Lansing, an Arabic speaker prayed: “O Allah, deal with those who besieged them. O Allah, deal with the aggressor Jews. O Allah, count them in number and kill them dispersed, and leave not one of them.” A speaker at the Islamic Center of America prayed that “Zionists” would be “cut … limb from limb.” More than 90 statements “pray for the mujahideen or call for jihad, at 16 of the 36 institutions.”

The overwhelming lion’s share of the taxpayer funds documented by MEF — more than $40 million — came from the Department of Agriculture (USDA) via the Michigan Department of Education in the form of school lunch dollars distributed to the Islamic Center of Detroit. Other funding sources included the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Health and Human Services (HHS), the state of Michigan, and local governments, such as the city of Detroit. The Michigan’s Islamist Pulpits site includes individual pages detailing the statements and (if applicable) funding of each of the Islamic groups. MEF clarified that “each institution received a request for comment before publication,” and their replies are documented in the database.

Notably CAIR-Michigan received more than $100,000 from the state of Michigan and the city of Detroit. During a talk on the “Dangers of Extremism,” a speaker at the CAIR-Michigan event told the audience:

When someone leaves the fold of Islam or commits treason then it is permissible for them to be killed but even still it’s not your decision or my decision it has to come from the sultan or the imam or the Amir al-Mu’minin, or if a judge, if a hakem or a qadi, then gives the hadd, gives the punishment for this. Just you or I just can’t say, well, someone committed treason, then we go shoot him in the head. This is Islam — respects the law and order. This would be un-Islamic. Islam respects law and order, dear brothers.

Tayeb Jukaku, the father-in-law of Muslim Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, is on CAIR-Michigan’s board of directors. Jukaku has backed El-Sayed with $300,000 in funding and is alleged to be a leader of a Muslim Brotherhood front group that funds Hamas.

“These are not anonymous voices on the internet. They are Michigan pulpits, in their own words, and many of them take public money and host public officials,” said Gregg Roman, executive director of the Middle East Forum. “The First Amendment protects a sermon. It does not entitle anyone to a state honor or a federal grant. Michigan’s leaders should stop funding and honoring these institutions until they have reviewed what is preached there, and every governor and every federal agency should ask the same question about the institutions they fund.”

MEF is proposing several courses of action to remedy the problem. The group calls on Congress to step in and investigate, holding “oversight hearings on federal money to institutions whose pulpits pray for jihad and for the killing of Jews.” In addition, MEF calls on the executive branch, specifically agencies such as USDA, DHS, and HHS, to clarify how they review grant subrecipients.

MEF also calls on state leaders in the executive and legislative branches “in every state” to investigate “which religious institutions receive schoolmeal, refugee, and security-grant money passed through their state, how those recipients are vetted, and which state officials have honored them.”

El-Sayed has appeared at a number of the mosques and institutions listed, such as the Islamic Center of Detroit and the Islamic Institute of America.
